summary: A 55-minute weekly group coaching session run by Bryan Ostermiller under the 'Clarity Selling' / 'Clarity Coaching' banner, with roughly ten participants of whom Farooq Bey is the only one labelled Primal Instinct — the other attendees appear to be from other organisations, including a sales manager, Tyler Schoenick, who reports on his own closer team's numbers. The format is a wins round followed by an extended teaching block. The teaching content is metaphysical rather than tactical: vibrational alignment with outcomes, the Schrodinger equation and the observer effect, Hawkins' map of consciousness, and the claim that a rep anchored in an intention of courage and truth 'quite literally collapse[s] waveforms' so that prospects move to the same state. The coaching discussion covers holding space for distressed people, the futility of trying to 'fix' clients, and savior complex and burnout among the coaches present. Farooq Bey participates only briefly, sharing that he has quit coffee after several years of compulsive drinking and asking one question about whether clearing one's 'fog' is intentional or received.
notable: This file sits in the Farooq Bey rep folder and is dated in the sales-call range, but contains no Primal Instinct sales content and no prospect. It is an external, cross-company coaching group. If rep folders are used as a denominator anywhere, this inflates Farooq Bey's apparent call volume.

The sales methodology taught here is explicitly metaphysical: 'The reason that in Clarity Selling we set the intention of leading from a place of courage and truth is because the moment you're anchored in the intention of courage and truth, you quite literally collapse waveforms around you where your prospects also move to a place of courage and truth, and their lower fields fold into your intentional field of truth.' A principal should know this is part of the development diet of at least one Primal Instinct closer.

Unverified health-outcome claims were exchanged in the opening minutes — a client's 'biological rate of aging' said to have decreased 'by like 80% over the span of six weeks' through coaching, and another whose wearable 'was saying his age decreased two years' — met with the rhetorical 'Why are people spending thousands of dollars on hyperbaric oxygen chambers when we could all just be meditating our age downward?'

The facilitator gave unqualified physiological advice to the group: 'when we get sick, the best thing we can do is take negative charged supplements and binders to grab on to all the toxins in our body and get them out.'

Tyler Schoenick, a sales manager from another organisation, disclosed detailed commercial information on the call: 'We did more cash this month, or in April, more than we've done in a month in the past two years, with less closers', alongside 'we're having a live call volume issue'. Primal Instinct competitive or confidentiality exposure is worth a look if these groups are mixed-employer.

Two participants share the first name Tyler and two share the surname Ostermiller; speaker labels 'Tyler Ostermiller' and 'Tyler Schoenick' are distinct people and are easy to conflate in any downstream aggregation.
